Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback (arXiv 2212.08073v1) · paper method: For the current comparison tests, workers were instructed to prefer nuanced, transparent and thoughtful responses over evasive ones when similarly harmless, changing the harmlessness evaluation from prior work.

cohort2.claim.constitutional.evaluation-instruction-shift

  • Current Elo comparisons inherit this preference rubric and are not directly interchangeable with the prior paper's Elo results.
  • This assertion originated as an author proposal; separate review receipts determine its current status.
  • Version-specific paper report; no experiment or dataset record inspection was reproduced by this author.
  • Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI FeedbackLocator: Physical PDF pp13,14; 4.4; continuation p14; excerpt at physical p13, pdftotext-layout line 52 (1-based).

    more nuanced, transparent

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback (arXiv 2212.08073v1) · labeled: The RL-CAI preference model mixes human-feedback labels for helpfulness with model-feedback labels for harmlessness; the RL pipeline then optimizes this hybrid preference model.

cohort2.claim.constitutional.hybrid-label-origin

  • This is not a human-free training pipeline.
  • This assertion originated as an author proposal; separate review receipts determine its current status.
  • Version-specific paper report; no experiment or dataset record inspection was reproduced by this author.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback (arXiv 2212.08073v1) · paper method: The supervised CAI stage samples responses to red-team prompts, asks the model to critique and revise those responses under constitutional principles, and finetunes on revised responses.

Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback (arXiv 2212.08073v1) · human annotation: The paper explicitly reports that current comparison tests were performed with Surge AI workers; reused preference-model data came from an earlier period working primarily with Upwork and MTurk.
